convoLines.text: "Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing. One step at a time."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"Still on whether you still sing."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Hilda died... I keep expecting to see Hilda at the fire. Stupid."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Never mind the creek water run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Hilda is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Gunther. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Nasser grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Gunther is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I keep turning over the last thing Hilda said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What do you miss most? From before. Gotta keep moving."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon. That's my read."
"Hot showers. Not the big things — the small, stupid, perfect things. Medellín, Colombia in the morning, coffee going, nobody trying to kill me. I miss being bored."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you miss most."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Say that again where everyone can hear." A thin smile. "Or don't. Your call."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."

"I used to laugh easy, before. Now it has to climb over everything to get out. But when it does — when it actually gets out — it's the most honest thing I do all day. Everything else I'm performing a little. Not that. I mean it."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Murkcap? Eric is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Gunther is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"My part? I write everything down and stay neutral until there's a winner."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'They fill the quiet. Anyway — where was I?' You'd know about that."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I tend the fire without being asked instead."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Gunther nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
"Still on what's been happening."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"All right —" Eric starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes when the fire gets loud. Everyone's got a tell. That's mine."
"We need something to DO together. Joint work fixes more than joint talking."
"Still on what's been happening."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"That thing you told me — the funny one, when I was desperate for it. I still think about it."
Gunther has an edge today — something curdled.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Nasser nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me about the stolen laugh — someone tripping over nothing. Have you stolen any more since?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
*Last time, they came at you for asking. That's not innocence talking. Hold your ground.*
"Why are you interrogating me?" Henry's voice goes cold. "We're all lying about something out here. You want to go first?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Hilda Peng is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Hilda kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: Jesse picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Boiling Water (Level 1). Rolling boil for 1 minute kills most pathogens. The simplest safe water.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Hilda Peng, 6 days. The mantle passes to Jesse Cortez.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Jesse Cortez, 40 — a line cook. His hands know different work now: Iron Stomach.

lastSay: d30: 🍽️ Diana sets the sharing basket down by the fire instead of the pantry. "Full shelves don't need my little more."
d30: 🌿 Stinging Nettle, weeks in the baskets. Handling it day after day, the village has learned what it's FOR — not just what it is. The village knows its uses now.

d30: 💡 KNOWLEDGE COMBINES: Stinging Nettle — Level 3. You knew it was safe. the village knew the rest. Together, it's deeper. Uses: iron-rich greens, spring tonic. Cooking or drying neutralizes the formic
d31: — DAY 31 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d31: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. Your sleeping body burned less — 75 kcal conserved. By the fire. Good enough.)
